headline: Constellation crushes earnings ($5.06 vs $3.89 expected) and nudges guidance up; KKR, NRG, Ferguson and Barrick report too; Rocket Lab, Take-Two and Occidental tonight
top_call: Constellation Energy, the nuclear-and-gas power giant that keeps signing AI data center deals, earned $5.06 a share vs about $3.89 expected, raised the midpoint of its 2026 guidance and added Amazon, Google and a $5 billion DOE loan commitment to the scoreboard. KKR beat on record fees, NRG beat by a mile but guided 2027 under Wall Street, and Ferguson beat and raised. Plain-English explainers below, plus who reports tonight.
subject: The Daily Five — Mon Nov 9: Constellation beats big ($5.06 vs $3.89) and raises
backdrop: Friday's bounce: the S&P 500 rose 0.3% and the Nasdaq gained 1.1% as Nvidia climbed 2.8% after two days of AI-led selling, while the Dow slipped 237 points (0.5%). The S&P still lost 2.7% on the week, its worst week since the April 2025 tariff shock, per AP.
on_deck_sub: Who reports after the close today, Nov 9, and what Wall Street expects (EPS estimates per Yahoo Finance)

ai.headline: Anthropic reportedly locked in $3.4 billion of gas-turbine generator orders (about 1.7 gigawatts) for future AI data centers, taking over existing orders from Texas-based OnePWR Solutions, per the Financial Times
ai.why: Constellation's earnings call and Anthropic's shopping list are the same story: power is the bottleneck. Neither company had confirmed the deal when Reuters reported it.

ai.headline: Trump said he doesn't mind AI guardrails and could work with Democrats on safeguards, while warning regulation shouldn't leave the US behind China
ai.why: The AI trade just had a rough week; a policy that is 'open to guardrails' is a headline the market will read both ways.

ai.headline: Alibaba's real-world coding-agent test found the top model fully completed only 26.4% of selected tasks, even as the same kinds of models score above 99% on older benchmarks
ai.why: The robots are great at tests and still mediocre at Mondays. Agent hype vs. agent reality, in one number.
